title: Error
description: A structured failure report. The schema exists so that failures stay distinguishable: Amasario requires that a network failure, an absent resource, an unsupported question and a malformed document are never collapsed into one generic error and never converted into an empty result. The category field is the mechanism, and the retryable field states whether retrying could plausibly succeed rather than leaving a consumer to guess.

code.description: A stable machine-readable code, namespaced by category, for example NETWORK_TIMEOUT or SPEC_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE. Stable so that a consumer can branch on it without matching on prose.

category.description: The failure domain. Separating these is the whole point of the schema: a consumer must be able to tell 'the network did not answer' from 'the answer was that nothing exists', because the two lead to opposite conclusions.

message.description: A human-readable explanation. Must not be the only information available: a consumer that has only the message cannot branch reliably, which is why code and category are required.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same operation could plausibly succeed. Absent means unknown, which must not be read as false.

path.description: The JSON pointer or field path within the offending document, for validation and compatibility failures.

detail.description: Additional structured detail. Deliberately open, but bounded by the rule that no secret, credential, private key or personal data may be recorded here; see docs/privacy.md.

cause.description: The underlying failure, when this error wraps another. Kept as a nested error rather than a string so that a chain of failures remains machine-readable.

boundary.description: The observation boundary at which the failure occurred, for network and contract failures.
